e-4693.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
e-4693.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071448/assets/627d12115d61ddfdedf9db08330269de2137a23abceada977d039e90e5b88675.png)
What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_2 := R_2 +(- 4) \cdot R_1$ on $A?$
e-4693.worked_solution:
The operation $R_2:=R_2 + (-4) R_1$ means that we need to add $-4$ times the first row to the second row. 

Carrying out this row operation, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4+(-4)(1) & 2+(-4)(2) & -1+(-4)(3) \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -13 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-4694.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
e-4694.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071448/assets/82729e1d34174d58f01547b58aa63db28ec68a4e1964ef5cd127a2167ed4a722.png) 

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ on $A?$
e-4694.worked_solution:
The operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-4695.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
e-4695.problem:
Which elementary row operation could transform the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071448/assets/56fd7e343edf6c26f36718a30f899af6c8eaf0cad5f6b07c90ffa93c19df6346.png)
e-4695.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has been changed is the $2$nd row. 

Now, applying the operation $R_2:=R_2+1 \cdot R_1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4+1\cdot (-4) & 1+1\cdot (-2) & 2+1\cdot 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the transformation could be done by the operation 

$$
R_2:=R_2+1\cdot R_1
$$

or simply

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1.
$$

e-4696.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
e-4696.problem:
Given that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071448/assets/59ee8e91d058e347238320a2bd5496630f33534564f67f901d2ddf89000f0108.png) which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
e-4696.worked_solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$

$$

$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the second row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0+(-2)(5) & 4+(-2)(2) & 7+(-2)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(1)(5) & 3+(1)(2) & 0+(1)(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R1:=R1−2R2 means that we need to add −2 times the second row to the first row.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the second row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0+(-2)(5) & 4+(-2)(2) & 7+(-2)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(1)(5) & 3+(1)(2) & 0+(1)(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 2
before.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Consider the matrix C, given by C=[96−71−3−2−24−3]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on C? R2:=R2+3R1R2:=R2−R3

a
[96−7−59−11−24−3]
b
[96−7−143−4−24−3]
c
[96−73011−20−24−3]
d
[96−72815−23−24−3]
e
[96−72619−26−24−3]
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply the operations in order: R2 = (1,−3,−2) + 3(9,6,−7) = (28,15,−23), then R2 = (28,15,−23) − (−2,4,−3) = (30,11,−20). The other rows remain unchanged, so option c is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1+(3)(9) & -3+(3)(6) & -2+(3)(-7) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28 & 15 & -23 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28+(-1)(-2) & 15+(-1)(4) & -23+(-1)(-3) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 30 & 11 & -20 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 2
?

Consider the matrix C, given by C=[96−71−3−2−24−3]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on C? R2:=R2+3R1R2:=R2−R3

a
[96−7−59−11−24−3]
b
[96−7−143−4−24−3]
c
[96−73011−20−24−3]
d
[96−72815−23−24−3]
e
[96−72619−26−24−3]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R2:=R2+3R1 means that we need to add 3 times the first row to the second row.

  • The operation R2:=R2−R3 means that we need to add −1 times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

C=[96−71−3−2−24−3]R2:=R2+3⋅R1∼[96−71+(3)(9)−3+(3)(6)−2+(3)(−7)−24−3]∼[96−72815−23−24−3]R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3∼[96−728+(−1)(−2)15+(−1)(4)−23+(−1)(−3)−24−3]∼[96−73011−20−24−3]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option c. First R2 becomes (28,15,−23); then subtracting R3 gives (28−(−2),15−4,−23−(−3)) = (30,11,−20). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 1+(3)(9) & -3+(3)(6) & -2+(3)(-7) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28 & 15 & -23 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 28+(-1)(-2) & 15+(-1)(4) & -23+(-1)(-3) \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & -7 \\ 30 & 11 & -20 \\ -2 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

a
[2277−1323−1]

[22773−13169−3]

decision.explanation: Multiply each entry of row 3 by 1/3: (6,9,−3)/3 = (2,3,−1). Rows 1 and 2 remain unchanged, giving option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot 6 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 9 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the matrix A, given by A=[2277−1369−3]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R3:=13R3 on A?

a
[2277−1323−1]
b
[22773−13169−3]
c
[2277−131827−9]
d
[2323737−1369−3]
e
[23−17−13227]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The operation R3:=13R3 means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by 13.

Multiplying the 3rd row by 13, we obtain the following:

A=[2277−1369−3]R3:=13⋅R3∼[2277−1313⋅613⋅913⋅−3]∼[2277−1323−1]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot 6 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 9 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: R3 becomes (3,−1,9) + 3(−1,2,4) = (0,5,21). Rows 1 and 2 remain unchanged, giving option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ on $M?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3+(3)(-1) & -1+(3)(2) & 9+(3)(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The operation R3:=R3+3R1 means that we need to add 3 times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

M=[−1248313−19]R3:=R3+3⋅R1∼[1−2−48313+(3)(−1)−1+(3)(2)9+(3)(4)]∼[−1248310521]

verification.explanation: R3 = (3,−1,9) + 3(−1,2,4) = (0,5,21), while rows 1 and 2 stay unchanged. This confirms option c and the worked solution’s final matrix; its intermediate first row contains a sign typo.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ on $M?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3+(3)(-1) & -1+(3)(2) & 9+(3)(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the third row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $5$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+(3)(2) & 2+(3)(0) & 1+(3)(-1) \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ -9+(5)(2) & 0+(5)(0) & -4+(5)(-1) \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the matrix C, given by C=[121−90−420−1]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on C? R1:=R1+3R3R2:=R2+5R3

a
[52−4−190−120−1]
b
[72−210−920−1]
c
[12172−210−9]
d
[72−2−90−410−9]
e
[12172−220−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R1:=R1+3R3 means that we need to add 3 times the third row to the first row.

  • The operation R2:=R2+5R3 means that we need to add 5 times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

C=[121−90−420−1]R1:=R1+3⋅R3∼[1+(3)(2)2+(3)(0)1+(3)(−1)−90−420−1]∼[72−2−90−420−1]R2:=R2+5⋅R3∼[72−2−9+(5)(2)0+(5)(0)−4+(5)(−1)20−1]∼[72−210−920−1]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the third row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $5$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+(3)(2) & 2+(3)(0) & 1+(3)(-1) \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ -9 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ -9+(5)(2) & 0+(5)(0) & -4+(5)(-1) \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $N?$

Question 6
?

Consider the augmented matrix N, given by N=[1−21−121237−131]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R2:=R2+(−2)⋅R1 on N?

a
[1−21−1010−17−131]
b
[1−21−10−1017−131]
c
[1−21−10−5057−131]
d
[1−21−105057−131]
e
[1−21−101017−131]
Submit

decision.explanation: R2 = (2,1,2,3) − 2(1,−2,1,−1) = (0,5,0,5). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged, giving option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $N?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2+(-2)(1) & 1+(-2)(-2) & 2+(-2)(1) & 3+(-2)(-1) \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Consider the augmented matrix N, given by N=[1−21−121237−131]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R2:=R2+(−2)⋅R1 on N?

a
[1−21−1010−17−131]
b
[1−21−10−1017−131]
c
[1−21−10−5057−131]
d
[1−21−105057−131]
e
[1−21−101017−131]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The operation R2:=R2+(−2)⋅R1 means that we need to add −2 times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

N=[1−21−121237−131]R2:=R2+(−2)⋅R1∼[1−21−12+(−2)(1)1+(−2)(−2)2+(−2)(1)3+(−2)(−1)7−131]∼[1−21−105057−131]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms R2 = (2−2, 1+4, 2−2, 3+2) = (0,5,0,5). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged, so option d is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $N?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2+(-2)(1) & 1+(-2)(-2) & 2+(-2)(1) & 3+(-2)(-1) \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 7
?

Consider the augmented matrix A, given by A=[4−1965−6−1−91]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R1↔R2 on A?

a
[65−6−1−914−19]
b
[4−1965−6−1−91]
c
[65−64−19−1−91]
d
[−1−9165−64−19]
e
[−1−914−1965−6]
Submit

decision.explanation: Swap the complete first and second rows, leaving the third row unchanged. The rows become (6,5,−6), (4,−1,9), and (−1,−9,1), giving option c.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 9 \\ 6 & 5 & -6 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 9 \\ 6 & 5 & -6 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & -6 \\ 4 & -1 & 9 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 7
?

Consider the augmented matrix A, given by A=[4−1965−6−1−91]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R1↔R2 on A?

a
[65−6−1−914−19]
b
[4−1965−6−1−91]
c
[65−64−19−1−91]
d
[−1−9165−64−19]
e
[−1−914−1965−6]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The operation R1↔R2 means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

A=[4−1965−6−1−91]R1↔R2∼[65−64−19−1−91]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 9 \\ 6 & 5 & -6 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 9 \\ 6 & 5 & -6 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & -6 \\ 4 & -1 & 9 \\ -1 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}$ on $T?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $2$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2+(2)(1) & -2+(2)(3) & 1+(2)(2)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the augmented matrix V, given by V=[−19−2644679057]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on V?

R1↔R3R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3

a
[9057−5410−19−26]
b
[4467−109−7−19057]
c
[90575−581−19−26]
d
[90574467−19−26]

decision.explanation: First swap rows 1 and 3, making R3 = (−1,9,−2,6). Then R2 = (4,4,6,7) − (−1,9,−2,6) = (5,−5,8,1). This gives option c.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Consider the augmented matrix V, given by V=[−19−2644679057]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on V?

R1↔R3R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3

a
[9057−5410−19−26]
b
[4467−109−7−19057]
c
[90575−581−19−26]
d
[90574467−19−26]
e
[−19−26−54109057]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R1↔R3 means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

  • The operation R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3 means that we need to add −1 times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

V=[−19−2644679057]R1↔R3∼[90574467−19−26]R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3∼[90574+(−1)(−1)4+(−1)(9)6+(−1)(−2)7+(−1)(6)−19−26]∼[90575−581−19−26]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $M?$

?

Consider the augmented matrix M, given by M=[10230−2141−112]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R3:=R3+(−1)⋅R1 on M?

a
[0−21410231102]
b
[10230−2141−112]
c
[10230−2140−1−1−1]
d
[13910−3300111]
e
[0−2141023110−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: R3 = (1,−1,1,2) − (1,0,2,3) = (0,−1,−1,−1). Rows 1 and 2 remain unchanged, giving option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $M?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & -1+(-1)(0) & 1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(3)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the augmented matrix M, given by M=[10230−2141−112]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R3:=R3+(−1)⋅R1 on M?

a
[0−21410231102]
b
[10230−2141−112]
c
[10230−2140−1−1−1]
d
[13910−3300111]
e
[0−2141023110−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The operation R3:=R3+(−1)⋅R1 means that we need to add −1 times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

M=[10230−2141−112]R3:=R3+(−1)⋅R1∼[10230−2141+(−1)(1)−1+(−1)(0)1+(−1)(2)2+(−1)(3)]∼[10230−2140−1−1−1]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $M?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & -1+(-1)(0) & 1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(3)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix S into the matrix T, where S=[6001202004015030],T=[150302004015030]?

a
R1:=(−2)R1
b
R1:=R1+14R2
c
R1:=−14R1
d
R1:=R1−12R3
e
R1:=14R1
Submit

decision.explanation: Only row 1 changes. Multiplying (60,0,120) by 1/4 gives (15,0,30), exactly the first row of T, so option e is correct.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $S$ into the matrix $T$, where

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that changes the $1$st  row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] & \,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] \\  & =T.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}.
$$

after.html:
Question 11
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix S into the matrix T, where S=[6001202004015030],T=[150302004015030]?

a
R1:=(−2)R1
b
R1:=R1+14R2
c
R1:=−14R1
d
R1:=R1−12R3
e
R1:=14R1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the 2nd and 3rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the 1st row.

By considering the given row operations that changes the 1st row, we notice that S=[6001202004015030]R1:=14⋅R1∼[150302004015030]=T.

Therefore, the required row operation is

R1:=14R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that multiplying row 1 by 1/4 changes (60,0,120) to (15,0,30), while rows 2 and 3 remain unchanged. Thus option e transforms S into T.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
content.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $S$ into the matrix $T$, where

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that changes the $1$st  row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}60 & 0 & 120 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] & \,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 30 \\ 20 & 0 & 40 \\ 15 & 0 & 30\end{aligned}] \\  & =T.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}.
$$

Question 13
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix X into the matrix W, where X=[112−4−11216],W=[112039216]?

a
R2:=R2+R3
b
R2:=R2+4R1
c
R2:=R2+2R3
d
R2↔R3
e
R1↔R2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the 1st and the 3rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the 2nd row.

By considering the given row operations that modify the 2nd row, we notice that

X=[112−4−11216]R2:=R2+4⋅R1∼[112039216]=W.

Therefore, the required row operation is

R2:=R2+4R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option b: (−4,−1,1) + 4(1,1,2) = (0,3,9). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged, producing W.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
content.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $X$ into the matrix $W$, where

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}.
$$

Question 14
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix A into the matrix B, where A=[52−3−802105−5],B=[52−3−80221−1]?

a
R3:=15⋅R3
b
R3:=R3+R2
c
R2:=R2+(−310)⋅R3
d
R3:=R3+(−2)⋅R1
e
R2:=R2+R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the 1st and the 2nd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the 3rd row.

By considering the given row operations that modify the 3rd row, we notice that

A=[52−3−802105−5]R3:=15⋅R3∼[52−3−80221−1]=B.

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=15⋅R3.

$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}\cdot {R}_{3}.
$$

after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $U$ into the matrix $V$, where

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd row is the same in both matrices. The only rows that have changed are the $1$st row and the $3$rd row.   

By considering the given row operations that change both the $1$st and the $3$rd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & \,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =V.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}.
$$

Question 15
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix U into the matrix V, where U=[13264512−1],V=[12−1645132]?

a
R2:=2R3+4R1
b
R2↔R3
c
 R1↔R3
d
R2↔R1
e
R3:=R2+(−5)R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the 2nd row is the same in both matrices. The only rows that have changed are the 1st row and the 3rd row.

By considering the given row operations that change both the 1st and the 3rd row, we notice that

U=[13264512−1]R1↔R3∼[12−1645132]=V.

Therefore, the required row operation is

R1↔R3.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Given that
$C=[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 2 & \,2 & \,1\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{33}=0?$
after.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation    

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 2 & \,2 & \,1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 3 & \,0 & \,0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$

Question 16

Given that C=[2−4−20−14221], which of the following elementary row operations makes a33=0?

a
R3:=R3+12R1
b
R3:=R3+(−2)R1
c
R3:=(−1)R3
d
R3:=R3+R1
e
R3↔R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R3:=R3+12R1.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

C=[2−4−20−14221]R3:=R3+12⋅R1∼[2−4−20−14300]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=R3+12R1.

content.problem:
Given that
$C=[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 2 & \,2 & \,1\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{33}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation    

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 2 & \,2 & \,1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-4 & \,\,-2 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,4 \\ 3 & \,0 & \,0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}.
$$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
Given that
$S=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{33}=0?$
after.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

or simply

$$

Given that S=[1−11321113], which of the following elementary row operations makes a33=0?

a
R3:=R3−3R1
b
R3↔R1
c
R3:=13R3
d
R3:=R3−2R2
e
R3↔R2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R3:=R3−3R1=R3+(−3)⋅R1

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

S=[1−11321113]R3:=R3+(−3)⋅R1∼[1−11321−240]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=R3+(−3)⋅R1

or simply

R3:=R3−3R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a: R3 = (1,1,3) − 3(1,−1,1) = (−2,4,0), so a33 becomes 0.

content.problem:
Given that
$S=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{33}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

or simply

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.
$$

a
R3:=13R3
b
R3:=R3+12R1
c
R3:=R3+(−3)R1
d
R3↔R1
e
R3:=R3+(−2)R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R3:=R3+(−3)R1.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

D=[13−1043322]R3:=R3+(−3)⋅R1∼[13−10430−75]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=R3+(−3)R1.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given 
$D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]$,
 which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{31}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}.
$$

Question 19
?

Given A=[624−91−5840], which of the following elementary row operations makes a32=0?

a
R3:=(−2)R3
b
R1↔R3
c
R1↔R2
d
R3:=R3+4R2
e
R3:=R3+(−2)R1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R3:=R3+(−2)R1.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

A=[624−91−5840]R3:=R3+(−2)⋅R1∼[624−91−5−40−8]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=R3+(−2)R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e: R3 = (8,4,0) − 2(6,2,4) = (−4,0,−8), so a32 becomes 0.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given 
$A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{32}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Question 20

Given that X=[−8106083903], which of the following elementary row operations makes a13=0?

a
R1:=R1+(−2)R2
b
R1↔R3
c
R1↔R2
d
R1:=R1+2R3
e
R1:=(−2)R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R1:=R1+(−2)R2.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

X=[−8106083903]R1:=R1+(−2)⋅R2∼[−8−60083903]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R1:=R1+(−2)R2.

content.problem:
Given that
$X=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 10 & 6 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{13}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 10 & 6 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}.
$$
